column7: I'm from the future. Weird year, this one. Don't ask me how it ends, it doesn't matter. Moving on.
On the thirtieth of January, three million pages of Epstein files came out. Four weeks later, America bombed Iran. Unrelated...
Trump bombed Iran, got nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize, then bombed them again. Fingers crossed. Hope you placed your bets on Polymarket.
The only reason your petrol isn't a fiver is Xi Jinping. Who would have thought.
America has been bringing peace to Iran since nineteen fifty-three. They simply can't get enough of it. Oil, I mean.
Trump said: A whole civilisation will die tonight. I don't want that to happen, but it probably will.
Mutually assured inaction is holding the peace together, like a duct-taped Temu vibrator.
His anti-war campaign is looking better on Polymarket. For some.
The Pentagon asked for two hundred billion more. Lockheed got fifty-eight billion for missiles. Somewhere, Dick Cheney got rigor mortis in his pants.
Brown University added up America's wars since nine eleven. Only about eight trillion dollars. Only about nine hundred thousand people killed.
That money would have ended world hunger for thirty years.
At least Lockheed's shareholders didn't go hungry, and the Taliban are gone.
The world spends three thousand seven hundred and sixty-eight dollars a second on nuclear bombs. Maybe they should budget better. Cancel the Netflix.
Pull themselves up by their blood-soaked bootstraps.
Where I'm from, the energy's free. We got it the year we stopped paying for these. I'm not telling you which year.
Same thing in Venezuela. Oil, blah, blah, blah. Same shit, different toilet. I'm not doing this twice. Next topic.
Oh yeah. Farage beat a bin. Whatever. The clown show goes on.
In September the village of Piddington voted to leave the UK. The government wants to put twelve hundred and fifty male asylum seekers next door.
No, Russia was not involved. Ninety-two percent turnout. A landslide. This is where democracy fails.
I've got a feeling Piddington doesn't have Scotland's budget for endless referendums. I'm not even sure it's on Google Maps. It just says: some... field...
They're from Afghanistan and Iran, among others. You'll remember those from earlier.
Planes, Trains and Automobiles, except it's a dinghy and nobody gets home for Thanksgiving.
Anyway. People are angry. The only ones who got home rich were three companies. They made three hundred and eighty million.
Quick question: how many meal deals can that buy? Asking for a friend.
In the pandemic, the government wasted nearly ten billion pounds on P P E. That's two and a half billion meal deals. Next.
A court told one P P E firm to pay back a hundred and twenty-two million. The government says it'll chase them with everything it's got.
Which explains why it's got nothing. They're too busy arguing about H S 2.
Some people got through the pandemic on furlough. One baroness got through it on sixty million and a yacht.
It doesn't have heated flooring, though. Moving on.
A British minister is reported to have told Jeffrey Epstein a five-hundred-billion-euro bailout would be announced that night. Nothing silly.
They let Greece sweat for months. When Spain and Portugal started wobbling, they threw the fucking kitchen sink at it.
When you've got nonce intelligence assets for Israel in the loop, it's time for a new solution, lads.
Netanyahu's solution is final: invading Lebanon and the West Bank at the same time.
Makes you wonder why we talk about fake currency and made-up conflicts over rare earth minerals,
all the while A I is planning our downfall. Hugging Face is just the beginning.
What's next? We smoke D M T in a virtual-reality doomscroll simulator, to dissociate from base reality,
which is clearly fucked, and we should start again... Anyway.
H S 2. A one hundred and two billion pound train that does not exist. It may arrive in the near future: twenty thirty-nine is the latest estimate.
How do they get away with wasting a hundred and two billion pounds? Local man is concerned about how this links to migrants.
The government wrote off 6.6 billion pounds in one year. How did we not know?
It came out the Friday before a bank holiday, in a heatwave, on England squad day. You were at a barbecue. They were counting on it.
Thirty-eight degrees. The government banned barbecues. We drank half a billion pints. The oil companies made forty-seven billion dollars. Cheers.
So that year was full of nonsensical shit, huh? What to do about it? Well, I'll tell you. You just have to listen...
Inspiring.
